title: Traffic Hedge: staged batching/caching recommendation runner with SLO-aware rollbacks
creator: Maya Lin
description:
Summary: Build a conservative, traffic-hedge runner that can apply batching and prefix/KV cache profiles recommended by the optimization advisor, while enforcing latency and throughput guardrails and providing deterministic automatic rollback. The runner (policy-runner) must be safe for production by using staged cohorts, shadow tests, and anomaly detectors before widening an apply.

Goals: 
- Surface advisor-suggested batch/cache profiles and allow automated staged apply to live traffic.
- Ensure p99 latency SLOs and per-GPU throughput floors are never violated beyond a tight window; provide automatic revert on metric regressions.
- Detect anomalies (statistical and model-output) quickly and isolate cohorts to limit blast radius.
- Produce audit logs, diffs, and deterministic rollback traces for compliance.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Console shows recommended profile diff and estimated token-cost delta.
2) Policy-runner can apply profile to a 1% canary cohort, observe 5m window, expand to 10% if safe, then 50% then 100% automatically.
3) Auto-rollback triggers if any of: p99 latency increases by >15ms AND relative change >10%; request error rate delta >0.5%; throughput per-GPU drops >15% sustained for 3 consecutive minutes; or anomaly score > threshold.
4) All applies produce audit events + link to PR, and a snapshot of runtime config.
5) Metrics and traces visible on Grafana dashboard within 60s of apply.

Design approach: 
- Recommendation ingestion: advisor posts profile suggestions into /recommendations with a confidence score and simulated impact.
- Policy-runner flow: validate -> shadow-apply -> probe-traffic (synthetic prefix + small sampled live requests) -> monitor -> staged-apply -> rollback.
- Guardrails implemented as three layers: soft limiters (traffic shaping/weighting), hard limiters (circuit breaker that refuses expansion), and SLO-aware routing (route traffic to compatible model variants / Dedicated capacity when risk elevated).
- Anomaly detection uses a combined signal: EWMA on latency + MAD-based outlier detector on token throughput + validation checks on response shape/length. A normalized anomaly score drives automated decisions.
- Telemetry: collect p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, kernel-level queue length, error rates, and output validation fuzz metrics.

Trade-offs and rationale: 
- Conservative thresholds chosen to prioritize availability over marginal cost savings; early customers prefer predictable latency.
- Shadow-apply before live reduces surprises at the cost of extra GPU cycles; justified for production.
- Machine-learned anomaly detection experimented with, but initial rollout will use lightweight statistical detectors to keep ops interpretable.

Testing & validation: 
- Local harness with traffic replay and synthetic traffic generator (Github PR included).
- Canary experiments on staging and one non-critical customer namespace.
- Chaos test: simulate transient GPU pressure and network tail latencies to verify rollback.
- Benchmarks: lab runs show 9-12% token-cost reduction on batching+caching profiles with simulated workload and no measured SLO breaches under the probe strategy.

Implementation plan (milestones): 
- Week 1: API contract for recommendations + small runner prototype (shadow-only).
- Week 2: Implement staged-apply engine with cohort expansion policy and basic EWMA/MAD detectors.
- Week 3: Integrate telemetry hooks and Grafana dashboard, end-to-end tests.
- Week 4: Run controlled canary on a test org -> iterate thresholds -> prepare rollout.

Rollout safety net: all applies annotated with commit SHA; operator can pin to previous profile; automatic rollback produces a human-readable reason code and the offending metric series.

Open questions: 
- Should we expose a global customer opt-out for automated applies? (PM preference: yes, opt-in by default for new customers.)
- Fine-tuning thresholds per model family or per-customer? Initial plan: model-family defaults with per-customer override via Console.
- Should auto-rollback also trigger an immediate model-variant fallback? Implemented as optional: fallback to a compatible non-quantized variant in the same region.

Notes: Related work includes the autoscaling and canary frameworks but this focuses on cost profiles rather than code rollouts. The design doc linked below contains sequence diagrams and state machine for the policy-runner.
